subject: Token-level throttle signal and next steps for ForestBank

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>

Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 11 Feb 2026 08:42:00 -0800
Subject: Token-level throttle signal and next steps for ForestBank

Hi Alexei / Meera,

Quick heads up — we observed a spike in 429s and queued requests for ForestBank's account beginning ~08:37 PST. The issue surface was token-level throttling on hosted inference for very long requests (typically >8k tokens) hitting our shared prefix routing. Impact: roughly 6% of requests from your production cluster experienced transient increases in latency and 429s between 08:37–09:05 PST.

What we did (short):
- Temporarily exempted your API key from the aggressive per-account concurrency cap (rolled to 2x for the affected hour).
- Re-routed a portion of traffic to a warm dedicated pool to reduce prefix collision pressure.
- Began collecting KV cache diagnostics and token pacing traces.

Attachments: incident_log_20260211.json (traces), kv-cache-heatmap.png (heatmap of eviction spikes).

Immediate ask: please let us know if you saw any user-facing failures beyond retries (errors your app surfaced in logs). We can schedule a short call today if useful.

Next note: we will follow up with a short postmortem and proposed remediation plan by EOD.

Thanks —
Soojin Lee
Incident Lead, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

Date: Thu, 12 Feb 2026 07:30:05 -0800
Subject: Post-incident snapshot & next steps — ForestBank token throughput event (Feb 11)

Alexei / Meera — following up with the investigation summary and next steps. Apologies again for the disruption.

Summary (short):
- Window: 2026-02-11 08:37–09:05 PST.
- Observed effect: transient 429s and elevated latency for long requests (>8k tokens) routed through shared prefix pools.
- Root cause (high level): an unexpected KV-cache eviction cascade on a subset of our shared hosts caused disproportionate re-computation and token pacing backpressure; this manifested as temporary per-account token-level throttles firing for high-concurrency long-run requests.

What we did:
- Immediate: lifted per-account throttle for your API key and rerouted traffic to a warm dedicated pool (reduction in 429s within ~2–3 minutes).
- Short-term fix deployed: adjusted cache eviction thresholds and tuned GC parameters on affected hosts (rolled 100% of the affected machines by 23:00 PST on 2026-02-11).
- Validation: running a targeted synthetic workload that mirrors your token distribution; no recurrence across a 48-hour window.

Proposed next steps:
1) Confirm follow-up call to review Dedicated routing for high-token workloads and recommend config changes for your client-side retry/backoff.
2) We will publish a short statuspage entry (draft below) and provide a goodwill credit for the impacted hour (Ben to finalize).
3) Share engineering artifacts: incident_analysis_20260212.pdf + the incident trace bundle (attached).

Draft status page blurb (suggested):
"Feb 11, 2026 — Degraded token throughput affecting a subset of long-form requests. Impacted customers experienced increased latency and intermittent 429s; engineering mitigations were applied and traffic was routed to a warm pool. Full investigation and remediation steps have been completed."

Please tell us if that wording is OK or if you prefer different framing. Happy to hop on a 30-minute call; Ben, can you propose slots?

Attachments: incident_analysis_20260212.pdf

Best,
Soojin Lee
Incident Lead, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
